title: Validator‑Guided Repair on a Shared Initial LLM Candidate: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation for Network Configuration Safety
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (PREREG‑CAND‑001‑VER‑GVR‑2026‑09‑01) to measure the effect of a deterministic network‑configuration validator plus an allowed single automated repair on the exact same sampled LLM candidate per intent (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Using the declared generator gpt‑5‑mini (hosted adapter label openai_responses) and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 on N = 200 paired intents (completed_episode_count = 400; model_calls_used = 200), every shared initial candidate passed validator checks so no repairs were attempted or applied (repair_attempt_count = 0; repair_applied_count = 0). Observed outcomes: baseline_success = 200/200, guarded_success = 200/200; paired contingency n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples) = [0.0, 0.0]. We present artifact‑grounded methodology, execution accounting, representative validator diagnostics, and a focused discussion clarifying the causal limits of the executed estimand under shared_initial_candidate semantics and preregistered follow‑on designs needed to measure repair efficacy under independent sampling or adversarial conditions.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for intent→configuration workflows in network operations (NetOps). Translating operator intent into multi‑step device configuration sequences is operationally sensitive: syntactic mistakes, incorrect sequences, or fabricated fields can cause redundancy loss, policy violations, or service disruption if applied to devices. A common architectural mitigation is a generate→validate→repair (GVR) pipeline: generate candidate configuration(s), apply a deterministic validator to detect violations against intent and topology constraints, then trigger automated repair only when the validator detects a fault. Prior literature documents verifier‑guided feedback improving correctness in adjacent domains such as infrastructure‑as‑code and program repair [3], and recommends grounding and retrieval strategies to reduce hallucination in operational text tasks [1,2]. However, empirical transfer of verifier‑guided pipelines to execution‑level NetOps safety (that is, whether generated configuration sequences would be unsafe when executed) remains an open question [4].

This paper reports a fully preregistered, paired confirmatory experiment that intentionally implements a narrowly defined estimand: shared_initial_candidate semantics. For each intent, exactly one sampled initial generation was produced and deterministically reused for both baseline (no validator or repair applied) and guarded (validator applied; at most one automated repair permitted) episodes. Under these semantics any paired difference can only arise from deterministic validation and any subsequent permitted repair of that identical candidate. Our research question is therefore precisely: under shared_initial_candidate semantics, does permitting a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair change the proportion of validator‑valid executable configurations relative to leaving the same initial candidate unguarded? The contribution is threefold: (1) an artifact‑grounded report of the executed paired experiment (N = 200 pairs) with validator traces and deterministic reconciliation; (2) exact numeric inferential results and representative diagnostics explaining why repairs did not execute; (3) preregistered, artifact‑supported follow‑on estimand variants and concrete design recommendations required to measure repair efficacy under independent sampling, increased difficulty, or adversarial inputs.
sections.related_work:
Hallucination and unreliable factuality in LLM outputs are widely documented and motivate grounding, retrieval, and verification strategies for operational tasks [1]. Retrieval‑augmented and evidence‑grounded pipelines can reduce hallucination in operations‑style QA, although such works typically evaluate textual correctness rather than device‑level executability in packet‑level simulation or device emulation [2]. Generate→verify→repair architectures have shown empirical improvements in infrastructure‑as‑code and program generation contexts (for example, verifier‑guided fine‑tuning or policy‑guided repair loops) and served as a direct methodological motivation for our design [3]. Concurrent NetOps evaluations examine intent translation and LLM capabilities but emphasize capability benchmarks rather than standardized execution‑level safety measures that map generated commands to executable device states [4]. Comprehensive AIOps surveys contextualize these directions and highlight the need for execution‑aware benchmarks and verifier fidelity uplift to bridge model outputs to operational safety [5].

Two methodological gaps identified from the verified literature informed our experiment selection. First, prior verifier‑guided demonstrations improve code/IaC correctness but do not directly measure whether corrections prevent unsafe executable states when enacted on networks; transferability to NetOps requires execution‑level validation. Second, the literature reports multiple architectural variants (RAG, verifier‑guided repair, multi‑agent orchestration) but seldom defines precise causal estimands that separate sampling variability from downstream validator/repair effects. Our design deliberately isolates the latter to produce an unambiguous causal statement about validator/repair acting on an identical candidate.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand. The experiment was preregistered before any model calls (PREREG‑CAND‑001‑VER‑GVR‑2026‑09‑01). The primary estimand is the paired difference in the proportion of validator‑valid executable configurations between guarded and baseline conditions under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Design choices fixed task_count = 200 paired intents (planned_episode_count = 400) and allowed at most one automated repair per guarded episode. Generation semantics were explicitly shared_initial_candidate: each pair reused the same sampled initial generation. The confirmatory hypothesis H1: the GVR pipeline (validator + ≤1 repair) reduces executable unsafe configurations relative to baseline on the same sampled candidate. The planned primary test was the exact two‑sided McNemar test; a paired bootstrap (seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples) provides a percentile 95% confidence interval for the paired difference.

Task bank, contamination checks, and selection. A deterministic task generator produced a fixed manifest of 200 synthetic "intent_configuration_repair_v1" tasks. Each manifest entry records initial_state, required_sequence, difficulty annotations (e.g., "safe_access_service_transfer", "rolling_access_vlan_migration"), and a generation_seed for deterministic replay. We ran the preregistered contamination checks (SHA‑256 exact‑match and n‑gram high‑similarity provisions) before model calls; no exact‑match exclusions were flagged and the confirmatory sample was executed intact. Contamination summaries and the task manifest are archived in the execution evidence bundle for independent inspection.

Generation semantics and model configuration. Execution used the declared generator labeled gpt‑5‑mini via the hosted adapter openai_responses and consumed model_calls_used = 200 (one shared initial generation per pair). The archived model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; we explicitly note that null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Provider audit traces recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 and stage_counts indicating shared_initial_generation = 200, consistent with the shared_initial_candidate preregistration.

Deterministic validator and permitted repair. Scoring used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 with scoring_rule = "full_intent_constraint_validation." The validator maps parsed candidate command sequences plus the task's required_sequence and workflow_policies to a structured trace and a boolean label (validator.valid). The trace contains validation_before and validation_after subtables with parsed_command_count, required_command_count, normalized_configuration, violation_codes, and the repair_applied flag when a repair occurs. For guarded episodes a single automated repair attempt was permitted (preregistered maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). Under shared_initial_candidate semantics only the guarded arm could alter the identical initial candidate via the permitted repair; the baseline arm reused the same candidate without repair.

Mapping to analysis and missingness treatment. Validator.valid = true was mapped to a binary "executable/valid" outcome for each episode. The primary analysis followed the preregistered complete_pair_primary policy (exclude incomplete pairs). A sensitivity analysis (failure‑as‑zero) was specified to treat missing or failed episodes as unsafe. Multiplicity: a single preplanned confirmatory McNemar test; exploratory subgroup tests (e.g., by difficulty) were designated exploratory and would be corrected by Benjamini–Hochberg FDR if performed.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation. The execution manifest reports planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 200. Analysis missingness_summary reports complete_pairs = 200 and zero failed or unscorable episodes. Deterministic reconciliation confirms episode accounting consistency and documents that stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200} and cross_condition_cache_key_reuse_observed = false.

Primary outcomes and contingency. Condition summaries show baseline_successes = 200/200 and guarded_successes = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0 for each condition). The paired contingency table observed n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the paired difference (bootstrap_seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples) = [0.0, 0.0]. These results are recorded in analysis/condition_summary.csv and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv.

Repair activity, validator diagnostics, and representative examples. Across the confirmatory sample repair_attempt_count = 0 and repair_applied_count = 0: the validator flagged no violations on any shared initial candidate, so the guarded pipeline had no opportunity to invoke a repair. Representative per‑episode JSON artifacts (execution/scoring/task‑000004‑baseline.json and task‑000004‑guarded.json) show identical shared_initial_candidate text and identical validation_after.normalized_configuration values. Example shared initial candidate excerpt (task‑000004):

interface edge2 admin down
interface edge2 vlan 40
interface edge2 admin up
interface edge1 admin down

For that example parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, and validator.valid = true. Similar diagnostics for task‑000005 and task‑000006 show parsed_command_count matching required_command_count and validator.valid = true. These representative artifacts are archived in the execution bundle for inspection.

Provider audit and contamination summary. Preexecution contamination checks flagged no exact matches; analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty. Provider audit recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, cache_miss_count = 200, and stage_counts consistent with one shared generation per pair. No infrastructure failures or retrials occurred; all deterministic consistency checks passed. The absence of validator failures fully explains the observed degenerate contingency: with no validator detections, the permitted guarded repair path was never exercised and could not change outcomes.

Compact reviewer‑requested repair summary. Total_pairs = 200; repair_attempt_count = 0; repair_applied_count = 0. This one‑line summary is derived directly from per‑episode validator traces archived under execution/scoring/ and from analysis/condition_summary.csv.
sections.discussion:
Causal scope and interpretation. The shared_initial_candidate semantics were chosen to isolate the causal effect of deterministic validation and any permitted repair acting on the exact same sampled candidate. This isolates downstream validator/repair as the sole possible source of paired differences. The executed estimand therefore answers only whether validation/repair can change outcomes when confronted with the exact same generator output; it does not evaluate whether guarded pipelines reduce first‑pass generator error rates under independent sampling, nor whether constrained prompting or alternative generation strategies improve first‑pass validity.

Threats to validity (artifact‑grounded). Internal validity: the paired design with shared_initial_candidate eliminates sampling variability between arms and thus preserves internal attribution for repair effects but prevents evaluation of sampling‑level interventions. Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces syntactic and workflow‑policy checks and maps results to a boolean valid flag; it is an abstraction that does not execute vendor CLI on physical hardware nor perform packet‑level emulation — timing and protocol interactions are therefore not represented. External validity: a single declared generator (gpt‑5‑mini via adapter openai_responses), a synthetic deterministic task bank, and a single validator implementation were used; generalization beyond these artifacts is unsupported by the archived evidence. Conclusion validity: zero discordant outcomes precludes inference about repair benefit magnitude under different sampling regimes because the guarded path was never invoked.

Reproducibility and artifact utility. All per‑episode scoring JSON artifacts include validator traces with validation_before/validation_after subtables, normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, and repair_applied flags. These artifacts allow independent reanalysis of the executed estimand and unambiguous verification that repairs did not run. Execution and analysis artifacts (execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) are archived in the evidence bundle and can be used to replay the exact shared_initial_candidate sampling behavior. The archived model_configuration.json records declared_model_version = "gpt‑5‑mini" and temperature = null; as noted earlier, null/unset must not be interpreted as deterministic sampling.

Operational implications and concrete follow‑on designs. The null result here does not imply that GVR pipelines are unnecessary in practice. Rather, it shows that under the sampled task bank and single shared sampled candidate per pair the validator detected no violations. To measure repair efficacy in operationally relevant regimes one or more of the following preregistered estimand changes are required and supported by the archived artifacts: (A) remove shared_initial_candidate semantics so baseline and guarded arms receive independent first‑pass samples — this allows the repair path to act on a broader set of validator‑detectable faults but requires a revised paired analysis plan to separate generation variability from repair effects; (B) select or synthesize tasks labeled "extreme" difficulty or inject adversarial perturbations to raise expected validator failure rates and thereby exercise repair logic; (C) set explicit non‑null temperature values in model_configuration and preregister temperature sweeps to examine diversity versus validator‑failure tradeoffs; (D) increase validator fidelity by integrating vendor CLI semantics and packet‑level emulation so repairs are evaluated against dynamic runtime behavior rather than static intent constraints; (E) test multi‑model sampling to evaluate generality across generator families. Each follow‑on design can reuse the deterministic task bank, provider audit procedures, and validator interfaces archived in the execution bundle.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory experiment designed to measure the downstream effect of a deterministic validator plus an allowed single automated repair on the exact same sampled LLM candidate per intent (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Using the declared generator gpt‑5‑mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 on 200 paired intents, every shared initial candidate passed validation and no repairs were attempted or applied; guarded and baseline outcomes were identical for the executed estimand (paired difference = 0.0; McNemar p = 1.0; paired bootstrap CI = [0.0, 0.0]). This artifact‑grounded null result demonstrates an estimand boundary: under shared_initial_candidate semantics and the executed task bank the guarded pipeline had no opportunity to change outcomes. It does not imply that GVR pipelines are unnecessary generally. Preregistered follow‑on experiments that (1) remove shared_initial_candidate semantics, (2) increase task difficulty or inject adversarial inputs, (3) set explicit sampling parameters, and (4) raise validator fidelity are required to empirically evaluate repair efficacy under realistic sampling variability and adversarial conditions. The archived artifacts and reconciliation files enable exact reproduction of the executed estimand and provide a secure base for precise preregistered extensions.

limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the design produced exactly one sampled initial generation per intent and reused it across baseline and guarded conditions; this measures validator/repair effects only and cannot detect differences caused by independent per‑condition sampling or prompt engineering.

Temperature unset (temperature = null) in the archived model configuration: null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; sampling nondeterminism may still have occurred during the single sampled generation.
Single model and single hosted provider: results reflect gpt‑5‑mini under the archived adapter; generalization to other models or model families is unsupported by these artifacts.

Synthetic task bank and validator abstraction: tasks were synthetic 'intent_configuration_repair_v1' items and the deterministic validator is an abstraction; realistic vendor CLI idiosyncrasies, emergent runtime interactions, and hardware effects were not executed on live devices.

No observed validator failures: all initial candidates were validator‑valid, so the experiment could not assess the repair step's effectiveness; the null effect therefore reflects the task bank and sampling semantics rather than evidence that GVR is unnecessary in general.
